affordance_in_statement: The total number of available vectors m is exactly n - 1. You are mathematically guaranteed that if you were to include all m available vectors, their linear span would contain all vectors of the form e_i - e_j.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving wording change that removes this reduction: with m = n - 1 and full difference-span connectivity, the underlying undirected incidence graph is necessarily a tree. Re-presenting the guarantee can obscure it linguistically, but cannot defeat solutions that inspect the input graph.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Recognizes that the vectors form a weighted tree and computes the minimum subtree connecting all targets by rooting at a target and traversing parent edges.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The full-span guarantee together with exactly n - 1 vectors makes the incidence graph a connected tree.

common_affordance: The guaranteed connected incidence graph has exactly n - 1 edges, so it is a tree and the answer is the total weight of the minimal target-connecting subtree.

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: Treats the task as an MST or terminal-connectivity construction rather than the minimum connecting subtree of an already fixed weighted tree, so it does not correctly account for the fixed tree structure and shared paths.
Uses shortest-path-style distance processing, effectively combining terminal distances instead of summing each required tree edge once; shared portions of paths are mishandled.

recommended_edit: No single semantics-preserving edit is available: the shared reduction is forced by immutable m = n - 1 and the stated full-span guarantee. Any edit that actually defeats both survivors must remove or alter that guarantee, thereby changing the problem.
